jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

IT Portfolio Manager - ABM Industries About the Role

ABM is seeking a highly disciplined, executive-facing IT Portfolio Manager to lead a pillar portfolio of enterprise technology initiatives and serve as the Pillar VP’s portfolio chief-ofstaff and trusted advisor—turning delivery noise into decision-ready options, crisp recommendations, and measurable outcomes, while protecting leadership time and ensuring commitments turn into follow-through.

In our PMO operating model, portfolio managers manage the portfolio of work — not the project managers. Project Managers run their projects end-to-end as independent leaders; people-management and performance reviews sit with a separate line manager.

This role succeeds through influence and orchestration: shaping intake, forcing prioritization tradeoffs, unblocking delivery, and translating execution into decision-ready insights, financial discipline, and transparency for leadership.

Benefit Information:

ABM offers a comprehensive benefits package. For information about ABM’s benefits, visit 2026 Recruiting Flyer - Staff & Mgmt

Pay: $110,000-$155,000

The pay listed is the salary range for this position. Any specific offer will vary based on the successful applicant’s

education, experience, skills, abilities, geographic location, and alignment with market data.

You may be eligible to participate in a Company incentive or bonus program.

Responsibilities

What You Will Own Pillar Portfolio Leadership & Executive Decision Enablement

Own the pillar portfolio across PMO + non-PMO work from intake through outcomes; maintain a single source of truth and an exec-ready view (RYG health, key milestones, blockers, decisions) that leaders can absorb in minutes.
Produce concise briefs and pre-reads for the VP/CIO-Staff: clear recommendation (continue/defer/stop), options, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, decision owner, and the exact decision needed.
Operate as the Pillar VP’s day-to-day portfolio advisor: run the portfolio decision agenda, pre-brief the VP ahead of key forums, represent the VP’s intent in crossfunctional sessions when appropriate, and ensure every decision has a named owner, due date, and closure.
Translate portfolio, financial, and capacity detail into plain-English executive insight and strategic recommendations—avoiding PMO/technical jargon and framing decisions in the language leaders will act on.
Run a light but rigorous operating cadence that protects executive time: default to async updates; use meetings only for decisions; and do not bring items forward until the decision packet is complete (required inputs, clear recommendation/options, financials, risks/dependencies, and necessary SME/architecture/security input) so decisions aren’t delayed by ‘need more info’ or follow-up actions. Portfolio Shaping, Intake & Prioritization
Drive intake readiness: ensure initiatives have defined outcomes, sponsor, business case/ROI, total cost, resource assumptions, KPIs, required approvals, and a clear decision ask before consuming executive time.
Facilitate prioritization and sequencing based on value, strategic alignment, mandatory work, dependencies, fiscal-year timing, and capacity.
Make tradeoffs explicit and recommend what to start, stop, or defer so the portfolio remains achievable (and teams are not overloaded).
Partner with sponsors and PMs to decompose bundled asks into clean initiatives; route work to the right leader/forum at the right stage (idea → refine business case → approve); maintain clear owners, success measures, and delivery approach.

Dependency, Risk, Capacity & Delivery Transparency

Identify cross-project dependencies and timing collisions; coordinate across teams/pillars to resolve issues before they become escalations; maintain awareness of the broader IT portfolio and flag inter-pillar conflicts/tradeoffs early.
Maintain portfolio-level RAID and escalation paths; surface risks early with mitigation options and decision requirements.
Proactively communicate and escalate: concise status narrative, early escalation, and clear decisions/next steps.
Convert resource strain into executive tradeoffs: if we take this on, what slips; if we accelerate, what changes; if we keep everything, what breaks. Value Delivery & Financial Stewardship
Track benefits and value delivery (outcomes, not activity); identify quick wins, and recommend course corrections, de-scopes, or stops when value is at risk.
Own portfolio-level budget tracking and forecasting; align spend to priorities, flag variances early, and recommend reallocations to avoid trapped dollars and yearend surprises.
Clarify financial and fiscal-year implications into plain decisions (CapEx vs OpEx, earmark vs approval, carryover risk, purchase timing).
Drive continuous improvement of the portfolio system (templates, dashboards, data hygiene, governance) to make decisions faster—and build a culture of transparent metrics and radical prioritization. What Success Looks Like
Pillar leadership consistently receives concise pre-reads; meetings result in decisions, not “updates”.
A focused, prioritized set of initiatives with clear sequencing and capacity realism — fewer fire drills, fewer stalled efforts, and fewer “everything is priority” debates.
Accurate, trusted portfolio reporting (roadmap, budget, risks, dependencies, capacity) with minimal executive escalations.
Project Managers feel empowered and unblocked; issues are resolved via timely escalations, not permission bottlenecks.
Benefits realization is tracked and the portfolio is continuously pruned and optimized to maximize value across the fiscal year. Experience & Capabilities
5–10 years in IT portfolio/PMO leadership in complex, matrixed enterprise environments; program management experience is a plus, but this role is explicitly portfolio-level (prioritization, tradeoffs, governance, exec decision support).
Demonstrated success partnering with VPs/CIO-staff using executive decision packets, governance cadences, and transparent prioritization.
Proven ability to influence without authority across business, infrastructure, security, data, vendors, and delivery teams.
Strong facilitation and stakeholder management; builds and nurtures trust-based relationships, navigates strong personalities with diplomacy and backbone.
Expertise in prioritization/sequencing, dependency and risk management, and capacity-based planning.
Financial stewardship experience: forecasting, budget alignment to priorities, variance narratives, and funding tradeoffs.
Exceptional executive communication — can compress an ocean of complex detail into the right altitude for each audience (1-page briefs, dashboards, and clear decision asks).
Experience with portfolio tooling, reporting, and decision logs strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build and operate executive-facing portfolio dashboards and KPI sets with clear definitions, baselines, and targets that support decisionmaking.

Candidates with a track record of continuous improvement — building simpler, faster portfolio processes that reduce friction and increase adoption — will be strongly considered.

Qualifications

Certifications (Preferred)

PMP or PMI PgMP/PfMP preferred but not required Who Will Thrive in This Role
Executive-ready communicators who drive decisions with concise options and recommendations
Portfolio thinkers who enjoy prioritization, tradeoffs, and simplifying complexity
Relationship-driven leaders who navigate strong personalities
Disciplined operators who run cadences, maintain decision hygiene, and deliver nosurprise transparency Who May Struggle
Individuals who prefer direct authority over influence, or who need to “own” people to drive outcomes
Those who default to long status updates instead of clear synthesis and recommendations
Anyone who avoids hard tradeoffs (stop/defer) and expects senior leaders to selfserve in tools/spreadsheets instead of curating, briefing, and driving clear decisions.
Anyone who defaults to committee bloat, hides behind process, or equates progress with meetings—rather than driving crisp packets, real decisions, and follow-through.

About Us

ABM (NYSE: ABM) is one of the world’s largest providers of integrated facility, engineering, and infrastructure solutions. Every day, our over 100,000 team members deliver essential services that make spaces cleaner, safer, and efficient, enhancing the overall occupant experience.

ABM serves a wide range of market sectors including commercial real estate, aviation, education, mission critical, and manufacturing and distribution. With over $8 billion in annual revenue and a blue-chip client base, ABM delivers innovative technologies and sustainable solutions that enhance facilities and empower clients to achieve their goals. Committed to creating smarter, more connected spaces, ABM is investing in the future to meet evolving challenges and build a healthier, thriving world. ABM: Driving possibility, together.

ABM is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer that does not discriminate on the basis of any trait or characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law, including disability and protected veteran status. ABM is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you have a disability and need assistance in completing the employment application, please call 888-328-8606. We will provide you with assistance and make a determination on your request for reasonable accommodation on a case-by-case basis.

ABM participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. E-Verify is an internet-based system used to electronically confirm employment eligibility.

ABM is a military-friendly company proudly employing thousands of men and women who have served in the U.S. military. With ABM, you’ll have access to a world-class training program and ample opportunities to use the skills you developed while serving our country. Whether you’re looking for a frontline or professional position, you can find post-military career opportunities across ABM.

Project Manager

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Stripe’s mission is to build the economic infrastructure for the internet. Risk and Compliance Engineering builds products to lower Stripe’s financial and regulatory risk at scale, while retaining a best in class user experience. We build user-facing products, and backend platforms to ensure Stripe’s users are compliant with regulatory and financial partner requirements. We protect Stripe’s brand while also protecting the company from financial losses that can put Stripe’s business at risk. The Risk TPM team is crucial to driving programs to address these challenges.

What you’ll do

As a Technical Program Manager in the Risk and Compliance space, you will play a key role across engineering, product, and strategy to drive programs that span across the Risk organization and Stripe. You will be responsible for the successful definition, cross-functional strategy, planning and execution of large-scale technical programs that help to solve complex problems and empower Stripe and our users.

Responsibilities

Execute on technical programs that require deep systems and engineering knowledge.
Partner with Engineering Managers, Product Managers and other cross functional partners to define, scope, and drive large programs to conclusion.
Develop, implement, and iterate on program management techniques, frameworks, and KPIs to achieve goals with well defined success criteria.
Make substantial improvements to how the teams you work with communicate and operate to significantly increase the productivity and efficiency of the teams.
Define and produce high quality written proposals, communications and documentation.
Leverage data and acquired knowledge to drive strategic decisions at an engineering leadership level.
Create widely circulated plans, driving consistency, clarity and building alignment across teams.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of software engineering, systems engineering and/or technical program management experience.
Excellent analytical skills; you digest complex information and make recommendations.
You have a track record of providing program management during all phases of software development from kick-off to launch, demonstrating critical thinking, challenging the norms and thought leadership.
You have very strong written and verbal communication skills, building strong relationships with stakeholders, teams and senior leaders around the organization.
You can drive internal and external process improvements across multiple teams and functions and bring a wealth of experience, opinions, proposals and best practices.
Experience operating autonomously and leading large-scale efforts across multiple teams and functions, with stakeholders in different disciplines across time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in financial risk and compliance
SQL and python scripting and/or programming skills

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $157,700 - $236,500. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Clutch

We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars. Are you game?

Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car-buying experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse thousands of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee… and that’s just the beginning.

Named five years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s list of the Top Growing Companies in Canada and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50™ and Fast 500™ lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.

Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, British Columbia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by several world-class investors, including Altos Ventures, Canaan Partners, BMO Capital, iA Financial, and FJ Labs. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.

About The Role

Clutch is scaling fast, and we're looking for a Technical Program Manager to help lead that growth from the ground up. You'll join at a pivotal moment; new production lines coming online, major capital projects underway, and ambitious production targets ahead. You'll be the person who makes sure it all comes together.

This is a rare opportunity to build the operating rhythm for a company in hypergrowth: owning the integrated plan across engineering, production, and software, and driving cross-functional teams toward a shared goal with real authority to make it happen.

If you're excited by ambiguity, energized by fast-paced environments, and want a seat at the table shaping how we scale, this is your chance to make a lasting mark on a company redefining how Canadians buy and sell cars.

This is not a project coordinator role. You'll need enough technical and operational depth to challenge assumptions from engineering, production, and other groups alike.

Key Responsibilities

Own the integrated program plan across concurrent capex projects, opex initiatives, and production ramp targets. Be the source of truth that every function references, not siloed plans that collide on the floor.
Identify and resolve cross-functional dependencies and resourcing conflicts (e.g., a facility install and a production milestone competing for the same technicians or floor time) before they become firefights.
Drive tradeoff conversations to resolution with functional leads across Production, Engineering, Facilities, Parts/Supply Chain, and other teams.
Support resequencing work and use judgment to determine what can be resolved independently and what needs to be escalated.
Build and maintain a resourcing view alongside the timeline. Understand who is committed to what, where the pinch points are over the next 4–8 weeks, and flag true capacity gaps versus prioritization problems.
Use real production data, including throughput, ramp curves, and utilization, to build recovery plans when a program slips rather than waiting for a scheduled review to identify issues.
Maintain a visible risk and issue log and run a regular cadence with senior leadership for decisions that exceed your authority.
Push back constructively when tradeoffs are being smoothed over instead of surfaced. This role only works if conflicts get named, not avoided.
Coordinate multiple workstreams from planning through completion, ensuring timelines, resources, and priorities remain aligned.
Help establish scalable processes and operating rhythms that support Clutch's continued growth.

What We're Looking For

3+ years in technical program management, engineering program leadership, or a closely related role in a manufacturing, automotive, or industrial operations environment.
Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, multi-workstream programs where capital projects, operational changes, and production targets intersected and competed for the same resources.
Strong technical and engineering fluency, with the ability to challenge assumptions and hold your own in discussions with engineering, production, and other technical teams.
Track record of driving cross-functional teams toward decisions under real-time pressure, including escalating appropriately when consensus stalls.
Experience building or maintaining integrated planning tools such as Linear, Wrike, or similar platforms, along with resourcing views across teams.
Strong understanding of production environments, processes, and operational workflows.
Direct, low-ego communication style; someone who names hard tradeoffs rather than avoiding them.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams simultaneously.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity and changing priorities.
P.Eng, engineering degree, or equivalent hands-on technical background strongly preferred given the level of technical credibility required.

Why You'll Love It at Clutch

Make an Impact: Help shape the future of car buying and selling in Canada by leading a critical part of our customer experience.
Career Growth: Join a rapidly growing company with opportunities for leadership and professional development.
Great Team: Work alongside talented, driven, and collaborative colleagues who are passionate about what they do.
Competitive Compensation: Enjoy a strong compensation package, including salary and benefits.

Employment Type

New, Permanent Full-Time

Compensation & Benefits

Salary Range: $100,000–$140,000

Competitive Compensation Package, Including Salary And Benefits.

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Overview

Saronic Technologies is seeking a Program Manager to own the execution and delivery of Marauder, our 180-foot Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV) produced at our Franklin, LA shipyard. This is a flagship large-scale production program, and the Program Manager is accountable for its cost, schedule, scope, and customer outcomes from contract award through delivery and sustainment.

Marauder is built at production scale and fielded across a wide and evolving range of complex missions. The Program Manager must pair deep expertise in large-scale shipbuilding and rate production with an instinct for modular kits, payloads, and mission-package integration—understanding how a common hull is configured, re-configured, and sustained to meet diverse customer needs. This role owns the balance between production throughput and mission flexibility.

The Program Manager serves as the primary customer-facing owner of the program, partnering closely with the internal Saronic growth, engineering, production and quality teams. The right candidate brings the customer fluency to manage government stakeholders and contracts, the technical acumen to make technical decisions aligned to the customer needs and contract requirements, and the programmatic discipline to deliver a large, complex platform at scale.

Responsibilities

Program Ownership & Delivery

Own end-to-end execution of the Marauder program, holding accountability for cost, schedule, scope, and quality from award through delivery and sustainment.
Serve as a leader and owner of the customer contract, deliverables, milestones, CDRLs, and contractual obligations.
Build and maintain the integrated program plan, aligning productions scheduled, engineering milestones, and integration timelines to customer commitments.
Drive risk and opportunity management across the program, escalating and resolving issues that threaten cost, schedule, or performance.
Report program health, forecasts, and decisions to Saronic leadership and customer stakeholders.

Large-Scale Production Interface

Partner with the Franklin production team to plan and execute rate production of a 180-foot ASV, from long-lead procurement through hull construction, outfitting, and delivery.
Monitor build sequencing, work breakdown, and production milestones to protect throughput while meeting quality and acceptance criteria.
Monitor and mitigate production risks—supply chain, labor, tooling, and facility constraints—unique to large-vessel shipbuilding.
Coordinate with Quality and Production to ensure build configurations and acceptance events meet customer and contractual standards.

Kit & Mission Package Integration

Own the configuration strategy for Marauder across a variety of mission packages, kits, and payloads on a common production hull.
Partner with Mission Package Integration Managers to plan integration of bespoke and commercial-off-the-shelf kits into the production and delivery flow.
Balance production standardization against mission-driven variance, protecting throughput while enabling flexibility.
Ensure integration timelines, dependencies, and configuration baselines are reflected in the master program plan.
Capture mission-package lessons learned and feed them back into production and product roadmaps.

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary point of contact for the customer, managing expectations, requirements, and relationships across the program lifecycle.
Elicit and clarify evolving mission needs, translating them into actionable program and technical direction.
Lead program reviews, delivery events, and technical exchanges with government stakeholders, operators, and evaluators.
Deliver clear, concise program updates and after-action reporting to leadership and customer audiences.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct and synchronize a cross-functional program team spanning Production, Engineering, Software, Mission Services, and Forward Deployed Engineering.
Partner with Technical Program Managers to align technical execution with programmatic commitments.
Make and defend tradeoff decisions across capability, schedule, cost, and risk.
Drive disciplined configuration management across vessels, kits, payloads, and software versions

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Naval Architecture, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in program management of large-scale production, shipbuilding, or complex defense development programs. Program Management experience of Unmanned Surface Vessels highly desirable.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interface confidently with technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated ownership of cost, schedule, and scope on programs of significant size and complexity.
Experience managing production at rate, including supply chain, build sequencing, and delivery of large or complex hardware systems highly desirable.
Proven ability to manage government or defense customers, contracts, and deliverables.
Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time.
Secret security clearance eligibility required, active preferred.

Key Competencies

Can own a large, complex program end-to-end while balancing production throughput against mission flexibility.
Can connect production and configuration decisions to overall program cost, schedule, and mission outcomes.
Can translate evolving customer requirements into disciplined, executable program plans.
Leadership of high-performing, cross-functional, and distributed teams.
Established track record of clear, consistent, and correct communications with peers, leaders, and external stakeholders.
Comfort guiding customers through ambiguous or evolving requirements and shaping actionable solutions.

Physical Demands

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Occasional standing and walking within the office
Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports
Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies

jobs.description:
Engineering Program Manager – Embedded Software / Consumer Devices

Summary:

We are seeking an Engineering Program Manager
to support the development of internal software tools and manufacturing test solutions for current and future embedded consumer products. In this role, you will partner closely with software, hardware, test, operations, and cross-functional engineering teams to define, manage, and execute manufacturing test strategies that validate devices under extended stress conditions.
The ideal candidate combines strong program management skills with a solid technical foundation in embedded systems and hardware/software interactions. You will coordinate engineering deliverables, drive issue resolution, prioritize competing initiatives, and communicate project status to technical teams and executive leadership while helping enable next-generation consumer devices.

Key Responsibilities:

Define, schedule, track, and communicate software feature development and engineering deliverables across multiple cross-functional teams.
Coordinate development of internal applications, frameworks, protocols, and command-line utilities supporting manufacturing and validation.
Support bring-up activities for new SoCs, chipsets, sensors, and embedded hardware platforms.
Lead triage efforts by identifying issues, driving root cause analysis, prioritizing workstreams, and coordinating resolution across engineering teams.
Develop lightweight scripts and tools to analyze engineering data, generate plots, and support validation activities.
Partner with Hardware, Software, OS, Test Engineering, Operations, and Manufacturing teams to enable test strategies for new products.
Support new product development builds and engineering validation activities.
Provide regular project status, risk assessments, and executive-level updates while driving projects to successful completion.

Required Qualifications:

5+ years of experience supporting embedded hardware/software development.
Prior experience in Engineering Program Management, Technical Program Management, or Software Project Leadership.
Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong understanding of embedded hardware components and hardware/software interactions.
Strong background in computer architecture, bus technologies (such as I2C and SPI), and I/O protocols (such as PCIe and USB).
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills.

SMS is seeking a highly experienced Deputy Program Manager to provide senior-level technical leadership, strategic guidance, and operational oversight in support of AFCENT A6 enterprise IT services across the USCENTCOM Area of Responsibility. This position will serve as a key advisor for network operations, systems engineering, cybersecurity operations, mission network sustainment, and IT project execution supporting contingency and wartime operations.

AFCENT’s mission is to deliver combat-ready air, space, communications, and cyberspace capability for USCENTCOM, helping maintain security and stability throughout Southwest Asia. We support the AFCENT Commander, USCENTCOM, coalition and joint partners, and warfighters who rely on NIPRNet, SIPRNet, partner networks, and other command-and-control systems. The AFCENT NOSC program is focused on running and protecting a 24/7 enterprise network and systems operations, including cybersecurity, engineering, maintenance, and technical support, keeping the AFCENT’s theater communications and IT infrastructure ready, secure, and available to effectively execute the AFCENT mission.

Since 1976, SMS has specialized in modernizing legacy IT and sustaining complex enterprise environments for federal agencies. With the goal of building long-term partnerships with our customers, we invest in our employees by providing the training, tools, and support they need to keep critical missions operational, improve performance, and reduce risk. SMS is headquartered in McLean, Virginia, with offices and on-site operations at customer locations throughout the United States. For additional information on SMS, visit www.sms.com .

Submit your resume today!

CCNP

jobs.title: Physical Security Intelligence Manager
jobs.description:
Vanguard is seeking an experienced, independent, and highly motivated Physical Security Intelligence Manager to lead intelligence efforts supporting the company’s footprint across the AMER region. In this role, you will be responsible for maturing and leading a regional physical security intelligence program supporting Vanguard’s site security operations in the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

As part of a globally integrated intelligence function, you will provide strategic, operational, and tactical intelligence support to protect Vanguard’s people, offices, operations, and events across the region. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape a developing capability, refine processes and product lines, and contribute to both regional and global security outcomes within one of the world’s leading investment management firms.

Core Responsibilities

Threat Identification and Assessment

Monitor, assess, and report on physical security threats with the potential to impact Vanguard operations, including civil unrest, crime trends, targeted violence, terrorism, and geopolitical or social developments relevant to site security.
Produce high-quality, timely intelligence products including threat assessments, executive briefings, site risk updates, risk forecasts, and incident-driven reports. Act as the regional subject matter expert for AMER sites, with a focus on identifying threats and trends that may affect Vanguard’s U.S., Mexico, and Canada operations.
Translate complex information into clear, concise, and actionable intelligence tailored to stakeholders to support security operations, site leadership, and executive decision-making.
Deliver horizon-scanning analysis to identify emerging risks and anticipate future threat developments.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partner with Site Security, Executive Protection, Travel Security, Business Continuity, Investigations, and other stakeholders to develop requirements and deliver a best-in-class intelligence service.
Build trusted relationships with internal business partners and external intelligence, security, and law enforcement contacts.
Brief senior leaders and security stakeholders on emerging threats and security risks.

Intelligence Program Development

Build and mature intelligence collection, monitoring, assessment, and reporting capabilities for the AMER region, with an emphasis on scalable processes, consistent standards, and measurable service delivery.
Lead development of the region’s intelligence service offering, including regional product lines, stakeholder engagement routines, requirements management, and reporting cadences.
Establish repeatable workflows to support incident monitoring, site-specific threat assessments, as-needed executive protection support, and emerging threat escalation across AMER locations.
Identify opportunities to improve processes with technology, automation, and open-source intelligence methodologies.

People Leadership and Performance Management

Lead, coach, and develop a small team of analysts, fostering a culture of critical thinking, professionalism, accountability, and continuous learning.
Set clear expectations, provide regular performance feedback, and support career development within the intelligence function.

Required Skills And Experience

At least 5 years of experience in physical security threat intelligence, geopolitical analysis, or a related field, with corporate or financial sector experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience assessing physical security risks across the Americas, including risks relating to targeted violence, terrorism, civil unrest, crime, and site security operations.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including team development, coaching, and performance management.
Independent, proactive, and comfortable leading regional intelligence efforts while working across a globally dispersed team and supporting time-sensitive operational requirements.
Experience building intelligence programs, developing stakeholder requirements, and establishing internal and external partnerships that improve security decision-making.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and written communication skills with the ability to produce finished intelligence products with minimal oversight.
Ability to transform complex information into clear, concise, and actionable intelligence products for senior decision-makers.
Experience briefing executive and senior leadership audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Relevant professional certifications or advanced degree in intelligence, security studies, homeland security, international relations, criminology, or a related discipline.
Experience assessing security and reputational risk in a multinational private sector environment.
Experienced user of OSINT technology platforms and data visualization tools.
Professional network of industry, government, law enforcement, and security contacts.
Familiarity with intelligence cycle methodologies and professional training in structured analytical techniques and open-source intelligence collection. Ability to conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis to inform impactful products on threat trends and forecasts.
Experience supporting crisis management or incident response operations.
Previous experience maturing an intelligence program through the development of new processes or procedures.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

jobs.title: Information System Security Manager
jobs.description:
The ISSM provides dedicated strategic cybersecurity leadership and oversight for designated classified information system enclaves supporting the 25th Attack Group (25 ATKW). Unlike a hybrid or tactical operations role, this position focuses exclusively on system-level cybersecurity governance, Risk Management Framework (RMF) compliance, and continuous monitoring to achieve and maintain Authorizations to Operate (ATO). The ISSM serves as the primary cybersecurity technical advisor to the Government Authorizing Official (AO), Program Manager (PM), and Information System Owner (ISO).

Essential Responsibilities:

Serve as the formally appointed Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM) for up to four contractor-managed Information Systems (including RPA Low, ACN, Audio MLS, and RPA High), overseeing the full lifecycle of cybersecurity compliance and system accreditation in accordance with DoDI 8510.01, AFI 17-101 (RMF), and AFMAN 17-1301 (COMPUSEC).
Develop, maintain, and oversee authorization documentation, System Security Plans (SSPs), risk assessments, and continuous monitoring activities using both eMASS and Xacta workflow platforms.
Act as the primary interface with Government Authorizing Officials (AOs) and Security Control Assessors (SCAs) to present risk assessments, initiate ATO packages, manage Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and secure timely renewals.
Maintain rigorous oversight of vulnerability management, incident reporting, access control governance, and configuration management functions across assigned enclaves.
Provide oversight and guidance to subordinate cybersecurity personnel (ISSOs) to ensure security control implementation and mitigation efforts align with established baselines and mission requirements.
Provide contingency continuity support for tactical enclave cybersecurity (ISSO) activities during periods of workforce shortfalls or as critical mission needs dictate.
Report conditions that materially affect system authorization status or cybersecurity posture directly to the Government, translating technical risk into actionable mission risk.
Initiate exceptions, deviations, or waivers to cybersecurity requirements when operational impacts dictate, ensuring complete documentation and coordination with the AO.
Ensure all assigned personnel and systems remain compliant with applicable DoW/DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:

A BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, or equivalently relative discipline, from an ABET accredited or CAE designated institution.
Must have an active Top-Secret clearance with Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) eligibility. US Citizenship is required.
Active DoD 8140 / DoDI 8570.01-M IAM Level II or III Certification matched to ISSM responsibilities prior to hiring.
Minimum 3-5 years of dedicated experience in RMF package development, continuous monitoring, and acting as an ISSM or lead ISSO.
Demonstrated proficiency in navigating and managing ATO packages within both eMASS and Xacta. Experience with STIGs, SCAP, vulnerability scanning, and ACAS/NESSUS.
Knowledge of cybersecurity laws, regulations, policies, governance, and technical safeguards governing the use, processing, storage, and transmission of classified information.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to confidently brief senior government leadership (AOs, SCAs, PMs) on cyber risk posture.
Must possess and maintain a valid state-issued driver’s license.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in a Cybersecurity or related field.
Experience with DODM 5205.07 Risk Management Framework, and familiarity with RPA SOC/C4 ISR mission system.

Work Environment, Physical Demands, and Mental Demands:

Typical office environment with no unusual hazards, occasional lifting of 20 pounds, kneeling, standing, and walking, routinely sitting and constant use of speech/hearing abilities for communication, constant mental alertness, and must be able to work under deadlines.

Job Description

GENERAL JOB SUMMARY:

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM) to lead the security management and compliance activities for information systems supporting our organization. The ISSM will be responsible for ensuring systems are securely designed, implemented, operated, and maintained in accordance with organizational security policies, regulatory requirements, and applicable cybersecurity frameworks.

Description

TrueNAS is redefining enterprise storage by delivering proven data resilience, performance, and flexibility without the complexity or constraints of legacy solutions. As the most deployed storage platform in the world, TrueNAS already powers critical data storage infrastructure for businesses, research institutions, and government agencies across 140+ countries and millions of users. Whether you work remotely or on-site, you’ll be part of a team that values collaboration and meaningful impact - where people come before profit, and bold ideas drive the future of data infrastructure.

If you’re ready to help shape the future of enterprise storage, we’d love to connect.

Position Overview:

The Program Manager (Business Operations / PMO) drives high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that improve how the business operates—from new process design through vendor selection and enterprise software implementation. This role leads multiple concurrent programs, building structure in ambiguity and translating leadership intent into clear plans, decisions, and execution. You will partner closely with senior leaders and teams across Operations, Finance, IT, Support, Sales Operations, Product, and Engineering to deliver outcomes on time and with measurable adoption. The ideal candidate is a proactive self-starter with strong business acumen, executive-ready communication, and a passion for learning systems and technology.

Our environment is fast-growing and high-ownership: priorities shift, problems are complex, and teams rely on each other to deliver. Success requires comfort with ambiguity, strong judgment, and an ability to align stakeholders through clear operating rhythms and data-driven decisions.

This is an in-office role in our Makati office. The hours for this position are M-F 8:00 am - 5:00 pm PT.

Base Pay Range

The base pay range of this position is ₱218,923.08 to ₱246,307.69 per month. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible to participate in the Company’s bonus program with a target bonus opportunity of 10% of base salary annually, subject to the achievement of individual and Company performance objectives and the terms of the applicable Company bonus plan.
Please note that the provided range reflects the pay spectrum for positions within the same job category as the one to which this position belongs. The final offer will consider various factors, such as location, education, and prior experience, to ensure a comprehensive and fair compensation assessment.

TrueNAS offers a comprehensive package of benefits including health, dental, vision, paid time off, and stock options.

Expected Posting Timelines

This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, a maximum of 90 days.

The Day-to-Day

The essential functions and responsibilities for this position include, but are not limited to, the following. Other duties may be assigned as needed.
Own end-to-end delivery for multiple concurrent cross-functional programs, balancing scope, timeline, quality, resources, and risk.
Develop program artifacts: charter, scope definition, work plan, milestones, RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies), and communications plan.
Establish governance and operating cadence: steering committees, executive readouts, decision logs, and consistent stakeholder updates.
Translate broad leadership direction into structured problem statements, requirements, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions.
Lead vendor evaluation efforts: facilitate requirements gathering, draft RFP/RFQ materials, define scoring models, coordinate demos, and manage due diligence through selection.
Partner with functional owners to design and document future-state processes, ensuring clear roles, controls, and handoffs.
Drive software implementation planning: project plan, resourcing, integration considerations, data migration approach, and go-live readiness.
Coordinate change management: stakeholder mapping, change impacts, training approach, enablement materials, and adoption reinforcement.
Plan and execute testing (UAT), cutover activities, and post-launch stabilization, ensuring operational continuity.
Manage cross-functional dependencies and remove blockers by clarifying ownership, sequencing work, and escalating decisively when needed.
Track outcomes and benefits realization: define KPIs, baselines, targets, and adoption metrics; report progress and course-correct.
Facilitate structured workshops (process mapping, requirements definition, solution design, retrospectives) and drive clear next steps.
Produce executive-ready documentation: concise narratives, dashboards, and decision memos with clear recommendations.
Identify opportunities to standardize tools, templates, and program practices to scale execution across the organization.
Model high ownership and accountability, coaching teams on effective execution and communication practices (formal or informal people leadership).

Education and Experience

We have identified the following programs, experience, and knowledge that have helped others find success in this role at TrueNAS. We understand, though, that knowledge comes from many forms of learning and experiences. Above all, we consider a person’s potential impact in the role and value their unique path to this point in their career.
Required

5+ years of experience in program management, project management, business operations, consulting, or similar cross-functional delivery roles.
2+ years leading initiatives that include process design/implementation and/or enterprise software implementations.
Experience operating within structured PMO environments and helping peer teams adopt consistent processes and standards.
Proven track record partnering with senior leaders and presenting structured updates, risks, and decisions.
Hands-on experience creating and managing program artifacts (charters, work plans, RAID logs, stakeholder/comms plans).
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience in Business, Operations, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field.

Preferred

Experience in B2B technology, hardware + software businesses, or operational environments with complex workflows and handoffs.
Experience leading vendor selection efforts (RFP/RFQ, scoring, demo coordination, due diligence).
Familiarity with change management approaches and adoption measurement (training, communications, readiness, utilization KPIs).
Experience working with enterprise tools (project/work management platforms, CRM/ERP/helpdesk concepts, integrations).
PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, CSM, or other relevant program/project management certification.
Prior people leadership experience (direct management) or demonstrated informal leadership across teams.

jobs.title: Safety & Security Manager
jobs.description:
About Our Job

The Denver Public Library (DPL) isn't just a place to borrow books; it's a vibrant, essential hub for our diverse city. As a growing urban library system with 28 locations and over 4 million annual visitors, we're deeply woven into the fabric of Denver.

Join a team where your values align with your work. At the Denver Public Library, we're not just serving our community; we're building a culture guided by values that empower both our staff and the public.

Welcoming: We make our resources, services, and expertise accessible for all, recognize the inherent dignity in each person, and provide safe places where everyone can be themselves.
Curiosity: We foster a culture of exploration, innovation, and forward thinking by creating environments that support learning and growth.
Connection: We are neighbors. We foster relationships, listen and act to build and strengthen our community. We bring people together to share information, ideas, and experiences.
Equity: We work to change inequitable practices, structures and policies, and attitudes that drive them, to provide opportunities for every person in our community to thrive. As we do so, we actively examine our roles in perpetuating oppressive systems.
Stewardship: We are accountable to our community, using our resources responsibly. We lead with honesty and integrity, protect privacy and preserve and share the full history of our Denver community.

If you're passionate about service, community engagement, and creating positive change, we invite you to explore career opportunities with us. Come join a team that believes in the power of knowledge, connection, and equity.

Unrivaled Benefits

The City and County of Denver offers a competitive salary commensurate with education and experience. We also offer generous benefits for full-time employees which include but is not limited to: 

Four (4) Medical Plans, Dental, Vision Insurance 
Pension Plan for Life (employee contributes 8.45%, employer contributes 17.95%) and 457 (b) Retirement Plan 
PTO (over 3 weeks in your first year), quarterly wellness hours, and 12 paid holidays
CARE Bank, Family Leave Benefits 
Enhanced Work/Life Balance: Employee Assistance Program (6 counseling sessions per year, legal assistance, financial counseling, discounted recreation center passes), Employee Volunteer Program
Professional Learning and Development Opportunities; Courses and Career Development Resources ; Education Refund Program
EcoPass (unlimited free RTD bus/train rides) 
For more information please visit our website.

About Our Division

The Operations Division provides the critical infrastructure and support services that enable Denver Public Library to deliver on its mission effectively and sustainably. The division encompasses Finance, Information Technology, Safety and Security, and Facilities and Planning—each playing a vital role in ensuring organizational stability, resilience, and growth. Finance oversees fiscal stewardship, budgeting, and resource allocation to maximize impact and accountability. Information Technology drives digital transformation, system reliability, and data security to support innovation and efficiency. Safety and Security ensures a safe and welcoming environment for staff, customers, and community members through proactive risk management and emergency preparedness. Facilities and Planning manages the maintenance, development, and long-term sustainability of organizational spaces, ensuring they are functional, accessible, and aligned with future needs. Together, these sub-divisions form an integrated operational backbone that supports the Denver Public library’s strategic priorities and day-to-day excellence.

About Our Position

Denver Public Library is hiring a Safety & Security Manager to support a safe and secure environment for staff, customers, and the library’s assets. This is a critical role in taking safety, continuity of operations, and emergency preparedness to the next level in alignment with the library’s Strategic Roadmap.

The role will lead the functional and operational areas for the security and safety of our 28 and growing number of library locations. Critical success factors will be defined by ensuring there are appropriate resources available to resolve complex business issues; informing, creating and maintaining best practices for safety and security; and creating processes that ensure the accomplishment of performance standards. This role is critical in acting as an advisor and subject matter expert to Denver Public Library leadership on all safety, security and emergency management related matters. Leads the communication and implementation of the overall safety and security strategy for the organization.

What You Would Bring

Leads planning and operations of the Security Department whose primary role is to maintain a safe and secure environment for customers and staff and to prevent asset loss.
Designs and implements a comprehensive safety and security program that safeguards people and stabilizes business operations.
Provides departmental oversight including the creation and modification of policies and procedures, creating and maintaining performance standards, budgeting, planning, and goal setting.
Motivates employees and offers a work environment conducive to excellent employee morale.
Enforces all library policies with specific focus on supporting staff and customers with the Library Use Policy, Child Safety Policy, and the Computer and Internet Use Policy.
Negotiates behavioral agreements with customers in violation of the Library Use Policy. Creates and maintains strong relationships with multiple City agencies including Denver Police and Fire Office of Emergency Management, Risk Management as well as with the community and all staff.
Communicates effectively about issues and initiatives with customers, staff, volunteers and administration, working especially closely with the library’s Community Resources and other key Public Services teams.
Reviews and investigates major security incidents and makes recommendations for actions to prevent, mitigate or lessen the organizational risks now and in the future.
Develops and implements emergency preparedness, response and continuity of operations plans.
Conducts drills to prepare library employees.
Conducts audits, studies and/or research projects, within the scope of the functional area, prepares comprehensive reports that reflect findings and conclusions; recommends feasible solutions in areas that require attention or change, and implements approved recommendations.
Oversees and monitors the safety and security incident reporting system.
Develops and tracks a dashboard of security and safety-related key performance indicators.
Maintains and utilizes data in the incident reporting system to make decisions and to forecast future security trends by location, including the optimization of security personnel for the organization.
Conducts and/or provides support for ongoing safety and security audits. Utilizes and generates reports from industry technology platforms.
Facilitates the safety committee meetings with DPL stakeholders.
Assists with the disaster recovery plan by collaborating with the Director of Facilities and Capital Planning, updating plans and leading periodic table top drills to test the plan.
Maintains a thorough knowledge of non-violent crisis intervention and de-escalation techniques.

Minimum Qualifications

Education requirement: Bachelor's Degree in a related field based on a specific position(s).
Experience Requirement: Three (3) years of experience at the type and level of functional or operational management, which must have included management of professional individual contributors.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Criminal Justice or a related field.
Knowledge of investigative practices and procedures and security dispatch centers.
Knowledge of loss prevention, theft, search and Worker’s Compensation procedures.
Knowledge of security and life/safety systems and programming.
Knowledge of laws and City ordinances pertaining to theft, disturbances, assault and vandalism.
Skill in exercising quick, mature and informed judgment in reacting effectively to emergency situations.
Skill in the documentation of incidents and personnel issues.
Skill in reviewing and maintaining records.
Training and/or certifications from the American Society of Industrial Security (ASIS), FEMA, and/or Disaster Recovery Institute, or other safety and security organizations
Experience working in a public setting such as libraries, parks, or schools
Experience with and knowledge of non-violent crisis intervention, public health challenges, and de-escalation practices
Demonstrates commitment to Denver Public Library values of equity, welcoming, connection, curiosity, and stewardship
Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) trained and/or experienced

Work Environment & Location

The Denver Public Library's branches are the arms to the community—each a unique reflection of the dynamic, diverse communities we serve. At DPL, we pride ourselves on showing up and providing support whenever there is a need.

While you may be hired for a specific location, please know that we are hiring with the expectation that at any time, you may be required to work at any one of our branches based on operational needs. This allows our staff to experience the full breadth of Denver's communities and ensures we consistently deliver the highest level of service across our branches.

Additionally, DPL employees may be redeployed to work in other locations or capacities to support core functions of the library system during branch closures or other emergencies.

This position is based out of the Central Library in the Civic Center area of downtown Denver and parking is not subsidized by DPL.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are

Our mission at Quandri is to transform insurance into a trusted and delightful experience using AI. We are building the AI operating system for North America’s best insurance agencies and brokerages.

For the first time ever, we have the technology to fundamentally change how insurance operates, and the stakes are human. Better insurance means families protected from harm, businesses able to take risks, and communities more resilient when the worst happens. For insurance practitioners, the ability to deliver this level of service finally becomes possible.

What we do

Quandri brings deeply specific, vertically-focused AI to the industry’s most critical stakeholders:insurance agencies and brokerages.
Agents are the lifeblood of the industry, the place where most property and casualty insurance is sold and serviced. Yet operating an agency is harder than ever. Peak product complexity, accelerating consolidation, a deepening talent crisis, and the AI revolution are all reshaping how agencies work.

Quandri sits at the cutting edge of this shift, rebuilding how agencies operate one workflow at a time. We pair a deep understanding of insurance processes, systems, and data with serious technical capability and proprietary models, so the transformation is tangible and operational rather than aspirational.

We’re making insurance better for policyholders, while helping insurance brokerages deliver a better client service, grow faster, and harness AI so that they control the future of insurance distribution.

Why join us?

You'll join a fast-moving team with real ownership, direct access to leadership, and a genuine hand in shaping the company's next chapter.
We are headquartered in beautiful Vancouver, BC, backed by leading US and Canadian investors , and the recognition has followed:
LinkedIn’s Top Canadian Startups in 2024 & 2025
Deloitte’s Fast 50
CB Insights’ Insurtech 50 and Fintech 100
The Globe and Mail’s Top Growing Companies in Canada .

About the Role:

Quandri is looking for a Senior Revenue Operations Lead to own the systems, processes, and analytics that keep our go-to-market engine running. This role sits at the center of Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, Implementation, and Finance — designing the territory plans, tooling, and processes those teams rely on, and turning data from our GTM tech stack into decisions leadership can act on. It is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable deep in HubSpot's system and in a room with sales leadership shaping next quarter's territory plan.

What you’ll do:

AI-Enabled Operations
Identify and implement opportunities to use AI tools, to streamline RevOps workflows, documentation, reporting, and process design.
Champion practical AI adoption across GTM teams, building repeatable, well-documented workflows rather than one-off use cases.

GTM Technology Stack Management
Own administration, configuration, and optimization of the GTM tech stack, with HubSpot as the system of record for the GTM teams.
Manage the dialing and sales-engagement stack (e.g., Nooks Dialer), including setup, integrations, and troubleshooting.
Coordinate with the Product team on Linear as needed to keep GTM-related requests, feedback loops, and issue tracking connected to Product/Engineering workflows.
Evaluate, implement, and integrate new tools as the GTM stack grows, maintaining a coherent, well-documented tech ecosystem and clean data flow between systems.

Process & Systems Architecture Design
Design and document scalable processes and workflows for BDRs, Account Executives, Implementation Managers, Customer Success Managers, and the Finance Teams, from lead handoff through renewal.
Build and maintain the underlying architecture (HubSpot pipelines, properties, workflows, and automations) that supports those processes.
Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the customer lifecycle and lead cross-functional projects to resolve them.
Maintain playbooks and process documentation so teams have a single source of truth for how GTM operations run.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
Act as the connective tissue between Sales, BDR, Customer Success, Implementation, Marketing, Product, and Finance on all things GTM operations.
Partner with Finance on pipeline hygiene, forecasting inputs, commission-relevant data, and revenue reporting accuracy.
Partner with Marketing Operations on lead generation, nurturing, account-based engagement and coverage, and other higher funnel activities that ultimately connect with BDRs and AEs.
Represent Revenue Operations in cross-functional planning (territory, quota, headcount, and process changes) to ensure systems and data can support decisions before they're finalized.

Reporting & Analytics
Build and maintain dashboards and reports in HubSpot to give leadership real-time visibility into pipeline, forecast, and team performance.
Ensure data integrity across the CRM and downstream reports through regular audits, cleanup, and validation rules.
Translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for Sales, CS, and executive stakeholders.
Co-own with Finance ARR reporting (new business, expansion, contraction, and churn).

Sales Territory Planning & Execution
Design, model, and maintain sales territory plans, balancing account potential, capacity, and fairness across the go-to-market team.
Partner with Sales leadership on quota setting, book-of-business assignments, and territory realignments, and manage execution of changes in HubSpot.
Monitor territory performance and coverage over time, recommending adjustments as the business and headcount evolve.

The right person for this role will have:

5+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or CX/Customer Operations, in B2B SaaS.
Deep, hands-on HubSpot expertise is required, including pipeline/property configuration, workflows/automation, reporting, and administration. Experience with another CRM (including Salesforce) does not substitute for this requirement.
Demonstrated experience designing and documenting processes for AE, BDR, CSM, and/or Implementation teams.
Strong analytical and reporting skills, with advanced proficiency in Excel and/or Google Sheets alongside HubSpot reporting.
Experience with sales territory design and quota planning.
Experience owning or administering a broader GTM tech stack (sales engagement/dialing tools, and similar systems) beyond the CRM itself.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively across Sales, CS, Implementation, Marketing, Product, and Finance.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate data into a clear narrative for both individual contributors and executives.
Experience designing and building AI-driven or automated GTM workflows (e.g., agentic processes, HubSpot- and Claude-based automation) that eliminate manual work, not just experience using off-the-shelf AI features.
Experience operating in a fast-growing or scaling SaaS environment.

Bonus points if you have:

Experience with data enrichment tools (i.e., Clay).
Familiarity with Linear or similar product/engineering issue-tracking tools.
Experience in the insurance industry is a bonus, though not required.

Our guiding principles:

Customers at the core.
We put the customer at the center of all we do. At a basic level, we believe business success comes down to talking to customers and building something they want. We don’t listen to customers and just take what they say blindly, but we think critically about it and build what they need. Customers are the core of everything we do, and our business exists to serve them. We prioritize their needs over all else within the company.
Move with urgency.
There are times when we need to move slowly and deliberately, but we default to acting fast and with urgency. We slow down when necessary, but this should be a deliberate choice. Businesses become more lethargic as they grow, this principle is designed to fight this fact.
Be curious.
We understand the world by being curious and asking why. We aren’t satisfied with surface level understanding, and seek a deeper understanding of why things are the way they are. Don’t take someone’s word for it or the answer “because that’s how we do it.” Understand why and dig deep.
Excellence in execution.
We know that what separates good from great is a high level of execution. We commit ourselves to excellence in everything that we do, from delivering an amazing product to writing a great email.
Act like an owner.
We’re all owners of the business and act like it. We follow through on commitments, own our results and think long-term.
Fight for simplicity.
The law of increasing functional information states that systems evolve to become more complex over time. At Quandri, we believe there is sophistication in simplicity; as such, we intentionally fight for streamlined solutions and are committed to the uncomplicated.
AI-first.
We believe AI is a fundamental shift in how work gets done, not just a tool we occasionally reach for. At Quandri, we lead with AI, in how we build our product, how we run our operations, and how we think about every process and workflow. This isn't about replacing people; it's about unlocking them to do higher-value work.

Compensation and Benefits:

The range for base pay is $110,000 - $150,000
which is dependent on level of experience
Employee stock options, granted based off experience level upon hire and subject to a standard vesting schedule
Employee stock options based on experience level
Comprehensive health benefits, including $500 Lifestyle Spending Account
Four weeks of paid vacation per year
Work anywhere in the world for 60 calendar days of the year
Parental leave top-ups: 6 months for birthing parents, 8 weeks for non-birthing parents (up to $100,000 annual salary)

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Program Director, MQ-9 Global Sustainment!

This position is responsible for overseeing cross-functional efforts focused on the delivery and sustainment of MQ-9 products, solutions, training devices, and services for U.S. Government and international customers, and for ensuring supporting internal processes, tools, and business systems enable effective execution. This includes direction of teams providing logistics/sustainment program management, training system development, technical publications integration, and shared engineering and software support across MQ-9A and MQ-9B customer fleets.

Predator Mission Trainer and Predator Mission Trainer (+)
Virtual Maintenance Training

Sets vision, direction, and priorities for the MQ-9 sustainment and training portfolio, aligning team objectives with corporate and P&L strategies and driving a high-performance, collaborative culture across geographically dispersed teams.
Coordinates departmental and cross-functional teams to assign and prioritize tasks focused on delivering new or upgraded products and services, resolving resource conflicts, and balancing competing priorities across product lines and customers.
Develops and delivers executive-level reports, proposals, requirements documentation, and presentations; leads and supports DCS (Direct Commercial Sales) and FMS (Foreign Military Sales) proposal development for international MQ-9 customers, including management of proposal efforts.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
About Conduit Health

Conduit Health is transforming one of the hardest, most outdated corners of post-acute care — getting essential medical equipment and supplies into patients’ homes. We’re the first vertically integrated, AI-powered platform to unite ordering, telehealth, prescriptions, insurance, and fulfillment into one seamless experience. In seconds, case managers and providers can say “yes” to patients who would otherwise wait weeks — while we handle every step behind the scenes.

The Role

We’re looking for an Implementation Manager to optimize state launches, payor implementations, partnerships, or high-impact projects across the company. You’ll work closely with multiple teams to plug in where the team needs most. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape operations and expansion in a high-growth startup environment, working hands-on with industry leaders and driving impact across our patient population.

The Implementation Manager leads new implementations - state expansions, payor launches, and cross-functional initiatives - from buy-in through execution, reporting to the Head of Operations. Sitting on the DME Operations team, they own the project management of these launches and act as the connective tissue across Clinical Ops, Support, Payor Development, and Product, actively gathering deliverables to keep commitments on track and things moving. The role fills the gap between strategy and delivery: someone accountable for making sure new initiatives actually land, rather than stalling in the handoffs between teams.

Who You Are

Organization is in your DNA. You bring clarity to chaos, simplify complex details, and surface information for who needs it most.
Execution-Focused & Detail-Oriented: You know what is needed to take a project from 0 to 1, and you thrive in organizing both the small and big details.
Collaborative Leader: You get buy-in across teams and levels across the organization.
Project Management: You keep team members and to do lists on track to get us where we need to go.
Tech-Savvy & Efficiency-Focused: You use systems, tools, and metrics to drive continuous improvement.

Examples Of What You'll Do

Own new state expansions - from post-diligence handoff through go-live - building the launch plan, timeline, and punch list, and driving every workstream to its date.
Lead payor implementations and launches, coordinating the eligibility, credentialing, billing, and fulfillment readiness that turns a signed contract into live patients.
Act as the connective tissue across M&A, Clinical Ops, Support, Payor Development, and Product - chasing commitments, unblocking handoffs, and keeping launches moving when they would otherwise stall.
Build and own the source-of-truth launch and expansion trackers so everyone knows what is done, what is next, and who owns it.
Run kick-offs, surface risks early, and course-correct before a slipped dependency becomes a missed launch.
Potentially own the network contracting admin the land-and-expand model runs on, standardizing work currently split across the team.
Report against launch KPIs - on-time launches, states executed, payors launched - and turn what you learn into repeatable playbooks.

What You'll Bring

Organization and structure-building are your superpower - you turn ambiguity into clear plans, trackers, and detailed punch lists (eg via Miro, Figma, Excel, Asana, Jira).
Proven project management: you can point to an initiative you took from 0 to 1 and explain exactly what moved it (even if you did not do every piece yourself).
Stakeholder management and a track record of getting buy-in across teams and levels.

This senior-level role is responsible for directing all phases of medical equipment implementation, including strategic planning, procurement coordination, delivery and installation logistics, installation management, and support to activation and project closeout.

The Senior Implementation Manager serves as a trusted advisor and facilitator to healthcare clients and executive stakeholders leading multidisciplinary teams to ensure successful project execution, operational readiness and seamless integration of medical equipment into clinical environments. This role also provides mentorship to junior implementation staff and supports organizational process improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Project Leadership

Lead multiple large-scale, high-profile, and complex healthcare equipment implementation scope from planning through building activation and occupancy.
Develop implementation strategies, execution plans, and logistics that align with client’s project goals.
Manage multiple concurrent projects, priorities, schedules, and cross-functional teams.
Serve as point of contact for medical equipment logistics for all project stakeholders.
Provide leadership with recommendations and problem-solving strategies with key stakeholders to reach consensus and issue resolution.

Medical Equipment Implementation Oversight

Direct procurement coordination, equipment logistics, installation sequencing, commissioning, and activation activities.
Perform architectural and mechanical/electrical/plumbing utilities reviews to ensure proper infrastructure is in place to support medical equipment. Coordinate any issues to resolution with the design team.

Mentor and guide Implementation Managers, Coordinators, and project support staff.
Establish implementation standards, workflows, and best practices across projects.
Sets a good example for the internal project team with a proactive, problem-solving mentality.
Facilitate collaboration between clinical teams, contractors, architects, engineers, vendors, and operational leadership.
Support staff development, performance improvement, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

Vendor & Client Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with healthcare clients, equipment manufacturers, vendors, and consulting partners.
Negotiate implementation schedules, delivery timelines, and issue resolution with vendors and contractors.
Lead stakeholder meetings, executive presentations, and client reporting activities.
Ensure client satisfaction through proactive communication and successful project delivery.

Regulatory Compliance & Quality Assurance

Support compliance with healthcare regulations, accreditation requirements, infection control protocols, and safety standards.
Support vendor and owner quality processes related to equipment installation, testing, commissioning, and acceptance.

Lead implementation audits, lessons learned reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Financial & Operational Management

Support project close out as needed

Experience

8–12+ years of experience in medical equipment planning, healthcare project management, healthcare construction, or equipment implementation.
Experience working and interacting in construction environment.
Experience communication with diverse groups from C suite, clinical users, project leadership and construction resources.
Managing projects in different areas requiring travel for site visits that include multiple days and air travel
Proven experience leading large-scale healthcare facility projects including acute care hospitals, imaging departments, surgical suites, laboratories, and specialty healthcare environments.

Technical Skills

Advanced knowledge of medical equipment systems, healthcare operations, and facility infrastructure requirements.
Adept at reading architectural and MEP construction drawings and can interpret vendor site-specific drawings.
Strong understanding of healthcare construction coordination and activation planning.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, project management software, scheduling and equipment database systems.
Experience with BIM/Revit coordination, AutoCAD, and healthcare planning tools preferred.
Strong analytical, budgeting, problem solving, and reporting capabilities.

PMP (Project Management Professional)
Certified Healthcare Constructor (CHC)

Lean Six Sigma Certification
CPHIMS or related healthcare certifications

Team leadership and mentorship

Negotiation and conflict resolution
