new_jobs.description:
Who we are

Our mission at Quandri is to transform insurance into a trusted and delightful experience using AI. We are building the AI operating system for North America’s best insurance agencies and brokerages.

For the first time ever, we have the technology to fundamentally change how insurance operates, and the stakes are human. Better insurance means families protected from harm, businesses able to take risks, and communities more resilient when the worst happens. For insurance practitioners, the ability to deliver this level of service finally becomes possible.

What we do

Quandri brings deeply specific, vertically-focused AI to the industry’s most critical stakeholders:insurance agencies and brokerages.
Agents are the lifeblood of the industry, the place where most property and casualty insurance is sold and serviced. Yet operating an agency is harder than ever. Peak product complexity, accelerating consolidation, a deepening talent crisis, and the AI revolution are all reshaping how agencies work.

Quandri sits at the cutting edge of this shift, rebuilding how agencies operate one workflow at a time. We pair a deep understanding of insurance processes, systems, and data with serious technical capability and proprietary models, so the transformation is tangible and operational rather than aspirational.

We’re making insurance better for policyholders, while helping insurance brokerages deliver a better client service, grow faster, and harness AI so that they control the future of insurance distribution.

Why join us?

You'll join a fast-moving team with real ownership, direct access to leadership, and a genuine hand in shaping the company's next chapter.
We are headquartered in beautiful Vancouver, BC, backed by leading US and Canadian investors , and the recognition has followed:
LinkedIn’s Top Canadian Startups in 2024 & 2025
Deloitte’s Fast 50
CB Insights’ Insurtech 50 and Fintech 100
The Globe and Mail’s Top Growing Companies in Canada .

About the Role:

Quandri is looking for a Senior Revenue Operations Lead to own the systems, processes, and analytics that keep our go-to-market engine running. This role sits at the center of Sales, Business Development, Customer Success, Implementation, and Finance — designing the territory plans, tooling, and processes those teams rely on, and turning data from our GTM tech stack into decisions leadership can act on. It is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable deep in HubSpot's system and in a room with sales leadership shaping next quarter's territory plan.

What you’ll do:

AI-Enabled Operations
Identify and implement opportunities to use AI tools, to streamline RevOps workflows, documentation, reporting, and process design.
Champion practical AI adoption across GTM teams, building repeatable, well-documented workflows rather than one-off use cases.

GTM Technology Stack Management
Own administration, configuration, and optimization of the GTM tech stack, with HubSpot as the system of record for the GTM teams.
Manage the dialing and sales-engagement stack (e.g., Nooks Dialer), including setup, integrations, and troubleshooting.
Coordinate with the Product team on Linear as needed to keep GTM-related requests, feedback loops, and issue tracking connected to Product/Engineering workflows.
Evaluate, implement, and integrate new tools as the GTM stack grows, maintaining a coherent, well-documented tech ecosystem and clean data flow between systems.

Process & Systems Architecture Design
Design and document scalable processes and workflows for BDRs, Account Executives, Implementation Managers, Customer Success Managers, and the Finance Teams, from lead handoff through renewal.
Build and maintain the underlying architecture (HubSpot pipelines, properties, workflows, and automations) that supports those processes.
Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the customer lifecycle and lead cross-functional projects to resolve them.
Maintain playbooks and process documentation so teams have a single source of truth for how GTM operations run.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
Act as the connective tissue between Sales, BDR, Customer Success, Implementation, Marketing, Product, and Finance on all things GTM operations.
Partner with Finance on pipeline hygiene, forecasting inputs, commission-relevant data, and revenue reporting accuracy.
Partner with Marketing Operations on lead generation, nurturing, account-based engagement and coverage, and other higher funnel activities that ultimately connect with BDRs and AEs.
Represent Revenue Operations in cross-functional planning (territory, quota, headcount, and process changes) to ensure systems and data can support decisions before they're finalized.

Reporting & Analytics
Build and maintain dashboards and reports in HubSpot to give leadership real-time visibility into pipeline, forecast, and team performance.
Ensure data integrity across the CRM and downstream reports through regular audits, cleanup, and validation rules.
Translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for Sales, CS, and executive stakeholders.
Co-own with Finance ARR reporting (new business, expansion, contraction, and churn).

Sales Territory Planning & Execution
Design, model, and maintain sales territory plans, balancing account potential, capacity, and fairness across the go-to-market team.
Partner with Sales leadership on quota setting, book-of-business assignments, and territory realignments, and manage execution of changes in HubSpot.
Monitor territory performance and coverage over time, recommending adjustments as the business and headcount evolve.

The right person for this role will have:

5+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or CX/Customer Operations, in B2B SaaS.
Deep, hands-on HubSpot expertise is required, including pipeline/property configuration, workflows/automation, reporting, and administration. Experience with another CRM (including Salesforce) does not substitute for this requirement.
Demonstrated experience designing and documenting processes for AE, BDR, CSM, and/or Implementation teams.
Strong analytical and reporting skills, with advanced proficiency in Excel and/or Google Sheets alongside HubSpot reporting.
Experience with sales territory design and quota planning.
Experience owning or administering a broader GTM tech stack (sales engagement/dialing tools, and similar systems) beyond the CRM itself.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively across Sales, CS, Implementation, Marketing, Product, and Finance.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate data into a clear narrative for both individual contributors and executives.
Experience designing and building AI-driven or automated GTM workflows (e.g., agentic processes, HubSpot- and Claude-based automation) that eliminate manual work, not just experience using off-the-shelf AI features.
Experience operating in a fast-growing or scaling SaaS environment.

Bonus points if you have:

Experience with data enrichment tools (i.e., Clay).
Familiarity with Linear or similar product/engineering issue-tracking tools.
Experience in the insurance industry is a bonus, though not required.

Our guiding principles:

Customers at the core.
We put the customer at the center of all we do. At a basic level, we believe business success comes down to talking to customers and building something they want. We don’t listen to customers and just take what they say blindly, but we think critically about it and build what they need. Customers are the core of everything we do, and our business exists to serve them. We prioritize their needs over all else within the company.
Move with urgency.
There are times when we need to move slowly and deliberately, but we default to acting fast and with urgency. We slow down when necessary, but this should be a deliberate choice. Businesses become more lethargic as they grow, this principle is designed to fight this fact.
Be curious.
We understand the world by being curious and asking why. We aren’t satisfied with surface level understanding, and seek a deeper understanding of why things are the way they are. Don’t take someone’s word for it or the answer “because that’s how we do it.” Understand why and dig deep.
Excellence in execution.
We know that what separates good from great is a high level of execution. We commit ourselves to excellence in everything that we do, from delivering an amazing product to writing a great email.
Act like an owner.
We’re all owners of the business and act like it. We follow through on commitments, own our results and think long-term.
Fight for simplicity.
The law of increasing functional information states that systems evolve to become more complex over time. At Quandri, we believe there is sophistication in simplicity; as such, we intentionally fight for streamlined solutions and are committed to the uncomplicated.
AI-first.
We believe AI is a fundamental shift in how work gets done, not just a tool we occasionally reach for. At Quandri, we lead with AI, in how we build our product, how we run our operations, and how we think about every process and workflow. This isn't about replacing people; it's about unlocking them to do higher-value work.

which is dependent on level of experience
Employee stock options, granted based off experience level upon hire and subject to a standard vesting schedule
Employee stock options based on experience level
Comprehensive health benefits, including $500 Lifestyle Spending Account
Four weeks of paid vacation per year
Work anywhere in the world for 60 calendar days of the year
Parental leave top-ups: 6 months for birthing parents, 8 weeks for non-birthing parents (up to $100,000 annual salary)

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.
Role Overview
The Threat Intelligence Analyst will play a critical role within Axon’s Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) by actively monitoring the global threat landscape, conducting in-depth threat analysis, and enabling early detection of risks that could impact Axon’s rapidly scaling global footprint—including people, facilities, travelers, and operations. This role is central to the GSOC’s mission of protecting life, mitigating loss, and moving from a reactive posture to a more proactive, intelligence-led approach—anticipating, assessing, and actioning threats before they materialize. The analyst will bridge threat intelligence across physical security, information security, and cybersecurity domains to ensure unified situational awareness and risk mitigation.
Key Responsibilities
Continuously monitor global threat landscapes, focusing on civil unrest, geopolitical instability, extremism, and organized crime.
Provide near real-time threat intelligence to GSOC leadership, enabling informed decision-making and proactive risk mitigation.
Produce clear, timely threat assessments, advisories, BOLOs, and situational reports for stakeholders across global operations, executive protection, workplace violence, and event security.
Serve as a liaison between GSOC and InfoSec/Cybersecurity teams, ensuring cross-domain threat intelligence convergence.
Develop and maintain early warning indicators, risk models, and intelligence watchlists for high-priority regions and assets.
Support incident monitoring, threat validation, and escalation during crisis events impacting global facilities or personnel.
Contribute to development of GSOC threat intelligence SOPs and playbooks, integrating tools and platforms like Fusus, ZeroFox, Citizen, and others.
Assist in training GSOC staff on intelligence tools, procedures, and current threats.
Represent Axon in external threat intelligence exchanges and corporate security working groups.

Minimum Qualifications
3–5 years of experience in threat intelligence, physical security, military, law enforcement, or corporate security settings.
Demonstrated expertise in OSINT tools, social media exploitation, and global threat monitoring platforms.
Strong analytical and writing skills with the ability to create concise, decision-ready reports.
Understanding of the convergence between physical security, cybersecurity, and information security domains.
Experience with enterprise security risk management and incident command models
Ability to manage competing priorities under pressure, with discretion and professionalism.
Bachelors degree in criminal justice, Intelligence Studies, Homeland Security, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing detailed threat profiles for global regions, cities, and Axon site locations.
Supportive role in physical security site assessments, including Threat and Vulnerability Assessments (TVAs).
Familiarity with travel security programs and integrating threat intel into travel protocols.
Understanding of executive protection support and protective intelligence methodologies.
Experience with Axon security tech stack including Fusus, Dedrone, Skydio, body-worn cameras, and Citizen Enterprise.
Relevant certifications such as CTIA, GCTI, GIAC GSIH, or equivalent.
Knowledge of behavioral threat assessment and workplace violence prevention programs.
Experience supporting GSOC operations, global events, or major incident responses.
Prior experience or demonstrated willingness to integrate into an Incident Command framework, including a significant role supporting ICS-based response in security, military, law enforcement, or corporate settings.
Strong alignment with Axon’s mission to Protect Life and a commitment to supporting public safety and the greater good of the community.

* * *

The Opportunity

CACI has an outstanding opportunity on the JGASS II program for select Senior Geospatial Intelligence Analysts who want to make a difference in the defense of the nation by applying their talents and experience in a fast-paced, dynamic environment in support of the US Special Operations Command.
The opportunity is limited to those who have the operational and technical experience and skills to effectively apply geospatial practices in support of real-world operations.
You will be an integral part of a selective professional geospatial team that is directly part of the operational planning cycle to support mission success.
This position is in support of a Department of Defense (DoD) organization located in Fayetteville, NC.

Responsibilities

You will perform full-spectrum geospatial analysis in support of complex geospatial, topographic, and imagery problem sets in support of global real-world operations.
You will be required to communicate analytical assessments clearly and succinctly, both written and orally, and present analysis products from creative analytical techniques in an operational environment.
You will use their technical expertise and experience in Processing, Exploitation, and Dissemination (PED) of ground feature data and remotely sensed data, such as Multi-Spectral Imagery (MSI), Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), and Electro-Optical Imagery, to support the operational customer.
You will be required to work in dynamic fast fast-paced environments that require both team interaction and individual efforts.
You must be experienced in interfacing with both internal and external leadership.
Specifically, the Geospatial Intelligence Analyst will be responsible for fusing multi-disciplinary intelligence sources to provide accurate and timely geospatial analysis in direct support of multiple geographically dispersed DoD organizations.
You are the interface to the operational elements to ensure the operational commander’s goals are accomplished through the synchronization of the geospatial enterprise.
You will use your knowledge and intelligence acumen to provide critical recommendations to operational decision makers.
You will work the full spectrum of the problem set, utilizing advanced geospatial capabilities and techniques to complete the mission. You will be challenged daily to expand your knowledge and understanding of operational application of geospatial practices across multiple disciplines.

Qualifications

Required:

TS/SCI
6 years of progressive experience in operational and tactical level intelligence, performing complex and timely geospatial, topographic, and imagery analysis.
Experience in targeting, intelligence, or geospatial systems.
Proficiency in utilizing GIS applications and intelligence-related automation for analytical efforts and product development.
Broad understanding of collection processes and management.
Ability to perform geospatial processing and develop new methodologies to solve complex tactical intelligence problems.

Desired

Proficiency in integrating with other intelligence disciplines.
Working knowledge of how geospatial techniques support the Find Fix Finish Exploit Analyze (F3EA) targeting cycle.
Working knowledge of computer scripting languages such as Python, JavaScript, HTML, R, or SAS.

What You Can Expect

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

Pay Range

There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

$65,000 - $136,500

Vanguard is seeking an experienced, independent, and highly motivated Physical Security Intelligence Manager to lead intelligence efforts supporting the company’s footprint across the AMER region. In this role, you will be responsible for maturing and leading a regional physical security intelligence program supporting Vanguard’s site security operations in the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

As part of a globally integrated intelligence function, you will provide strategic, operational, and tactical intelligence support to protect Vanguard’s people, offices, operations, and events across the region. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape a developing capability, refine processes and product lines, and contribute to both regional and global security outcomes within one of the world’s leading investment management firms.

Core Responsibilities

Threat Identification and Assessment

Monitor, assess, and report on physical security threats with the potential to impact Vanguard operations, including civil unrest, crime trends, targeted violence, terrorism, and geopolitical or social developments relevant to site security.
Produce high-quality, timely intelligence products including threat assessments, executive briefings, site risk updates, risk forecasts, and incident-driven reports. Act as the regional subject matter expert for AMER sites, with a focus on identifying threats and trends that may affect Vanguard’s U.S., Mexico, and Canada operations.
Translate complex information into clear, concise, and actionable intelligence tailored to stakeholders to support security operations, site leadership, and executive decision-making.
Deliver horizon-scanning analysis to identify emerging risks and anticipate future threat developments.

Stakeholder Engagement

Partner with Site Security, Executive Protection, Travel Security, Business Continuity, Investigations, and other stakeholders to develop requirements and deliver a best-in-class intelligence service.
Build trusted relationships with internal business partners and external intelligence, security, and law enforcement contacts.
Brief senior leaders and security stakeholders on emerging threats and security risks.

Intelligence Program Development

Build and mature intelligence collection, monitoring, assessment, and reporting capabilities for the AMER region, with an emphasis on scalable processes, consistent standards, and measurable service delivery.
Lead development of the region’s intelligence service offering, including regional product lines, stakeholder engagement routines, requirements management, and reporting cadences.
Establish repeatable workflows to support incident monitoring, site-specific threat assessments, as-needed executive protection support, and emerging threat escalation across AMER locations.
Identify opportunities to improve processes with technology, automation, and open-source intelligence methodologies.

People Leadership and Performance Management

Lead, coach, and develop a small team of analysts, fostering a culture of critical thinking, professionalism, accountability, and continuous learning.
Set clear expectations, provide regular performance feedback, and support career development within the intelligence function.

Required Skills And Experience

At least 5 years of experience in physical security threat intelligence, geopolitical analysis, or a related field, with corporate or financial sector experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience assessing physical security risks across the Americas, including risks relating to targeted violence, terrorism, civil unrest, crime, and site security operations.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including team development, coaching, and performance management.
Independent, proactive, and comfortable leading regional intelligence efforts while working across a globally dispersed team and supporting time-sensitive operational requirements.
Experience building intelligence programs, developing stakeholder requirements, and establishing internal and external partnerships that improve security decision-making.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and written communication skills with the ability to produce finished intelligence products with minimal oversight.
Ability to transform complex information into clear, concise, and actionable intelligence products for senior decision-makers.
Experience briefing executive and senior leadership audiences.

Relevant professional certifications or advanced degree in intelligence, security studies, homeland security, international relations, criminology, or a related discipline.
Experience assessing security and reputational risk in a multinational private sector environment.
Experienced user of OSINT technology platforms and data visualization tools.
Professional network of industry, government, law enforcement, and security contacts.
Familiarity with intelligence cycle methodologies and professional training in structured analytical techniques and open-source intelligence collection. Ability to conduct quantitative and qualitative analysis to inform impactful products on threat trends and forecasts.

Job Description

Fusion Incident Management (FIM)

Department Overview

Fusion Incident Management (FIM) exists to reduce organizational risk and protect customers, colleagues, and the Bank by leading the coordinated response to significant fraud and information security incidents. FIM serves as the central command function that brings together fraud, security, technology, risk, investigative, legal, compliance, and other business partners to assess, contain, manage, communicate, and recover from high-impact incidents. The team provides a centralized enterprise incident management capability with 24x7x365 coverage, helping minimize operational, financial, regulatory, reputational, and customer impacts across the organization.

What you will do?

As a Senior Information Security Analyst within the Fraud Pillar of Fusion Incident Management, you will lead the coordination and management of complex fraud, financial crime, insider risk, and fraud-related cybersecurity incidents. You will play a critical role in protecting customers and the Bank by driving timely containment, recovery, investigation, and remediation activities while providing clear executive-level situational awareness and risk assessments. Your ability to remain calm under pressure, make informed decisions, and collaborate across diverse stakeholder groups will directly contribute to the Bank's operational resilience and fraud risk management objectives.

Job Details

Lead Fraud Incident Response:

Lead and coordinate enterprise response activities for significant fraud, financial crime, insider risk, and fraud-related cybersecurity incidents.
Drive containment, recovery, remediation, and closure activities while ensuring timely decision-making and action execution.
Track incident tasks, data, and workstreams.
Able to understand and ensure appropriate fraud detection, monitoring, prevention, and response controls are in place to address current and emerging fraud threats and fraud loss exposure.
Assess customer, financial, operational, regulatory, and reputational impacts throughout the incident lifecycle.
Provide incident leadership during on-call rotations and major incident events.

Enable Executive Decision-Making

Conduct incident severity assessments and provide risk-based recommendations to senior leadership.
Deliver concise, timely, and actionable updates to executives, stakeholders, and response teams.
Support crisis escalations and facilitate incident governance processes.
Maintain situational awareness and ensure stakeholders have the information required to make informed decisions.

Partner Across the Enterprise

Act as a central coordination point between fraud operations, cyber security teams, technology, investigations, legal, compliance, risk management, and business teams.
Drive alignment across multiple workstreams, ensuring accountability, transparency, and timely completion of response actions.
Provide subject matter expertise on fraud risk, fraud controls, investigative processes, and emerging fraud threats.
Build effective working relationships that support rapid and coordinated incident response.

Strengthen Fraud Risk Management

Evaluate the effectiveness of fraud detection, monitoring, prevention, and response controls during active incidents.
Identify risk exposures, control gaps, and emerging threats, recommending appropriate remediation activities.
Support regulatory reviews, audits, management responses, and control enhancement initiatives.
Contribute expertise to enterprise projects and strategic initiatives involving fraud and information security incident and risk management.

Drive Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement

Maintain accurate and comprehensive incident documentation as the single source of truth.
Support post-incident reviews, lessons learned activities, and root cause analysis efforts.
Identify opportunities to improve incident management processes, governance, and operational effectiveness.
Promote collaborative team culture and contribute to knowledge sharing across the organization.

Where you will work?

This role operates within a highly collaborative enterprise incident management environment and participates in a 24x7x365 follow-the-sun and on-call support model. Team members work closely with partners across Fraud, Cyber Security, Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Investigations to manage incidents that may impact customers, business operations, and enterprise assets. Specific work arrangement details (hybrid, remote, or onsite requirements) will be provided by the hiring manager.

What you need to succeed?

Required Qualifications

University degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
4+ years of experience in fraud operations, fraud investigations, fraud risk management, insider risk, financial crime, information security, or incident response.
Experience leading or coordinating fraud investigations or incidents involving significant customer impact, financial exposure, regulatory implications, or reputational risk.
Strong knowledge of fraud typologies, including account takeover, identity theft, synthetic identity fraud, payment fraud, social engineering, insider fraud, and emerging digital fraud threats.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with executives and senior stakeholders during high-pressure situations.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Experience working within cross-functional teams and managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong understanding of fraud operations, knowledge of financial services fraud controls, fraud detection technologies, and fraud risk management frameworks.
Experience in enterprise incident management, cyber incident response, or crisis management environments.
Information Security certification or accreditation (Security+, CISSP, GCIH, CISM, GIAC, or equivalent).
Experience developing executive communications, incident briefings, and senior leadership reporting.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means effectively leading complex incident response activities, driving timely containment and recovery actions, delivering high-quality executive communications, enabling informed risk-based decisions, and continuously improving the Bank's fraud incident management capabilities. You will be recognized as a trusted partner who brings structure, clarity, and leadership during some of the organization's most significant fraud events.

Who We Are

TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing.
